pages.description: Ready-to-teach English presentation packs for the classroom projector: one deck a lesson, with the board work, examples and tasks already laid out.
pages.keywords: english lesson presentations, classroom slides for english teachers, powerpoint english lessons sri lanka, teaching slides, presentation packs

hero.text: Slides you can teach from without rebuilding them first: the board work, the examples and the tasks already laid out, in the order a lesson actually runs.

blocks.heading: What a presentation pack is
text: Each pack is a set of slides for one lesson or one unit, made to be shown on a classroom projector or a screen at home. The slides carry what you would otherwise write on the board: the target language, the examples, the questions, and the tasks in the order you will set them.

They are not a lesson plan with pictures added. A plan tells you what to do; a deck is what the class looks at while you do it. The two work together, and the free [lesson plans](teacher-resources/ppp-lesson-plans/) on this site tell you what a plan should contain.

blocks.heading: What is in every pack
bullets: **A title slide and an aim slide,** so the class can see what the lesson is for.
**The language, presented once and clearly** - the structure, its form, and two or three examples, on slides a child at the back can read.
**Practice slides in order,** from recognising to producing, with the answers on the slide that follows rather than in a separate file.
**A task the class can do** while the slide stays up, so nobody has to remember the instruction.
**A closing slide** with the homework written out.

blocks.heading: How they reach you
text: Packs are delivered as a link to the file in Google Drive, sent after payment. Nothing is downloaded from this website, and the site never asks for a card number: payment is by bank transfer, arranged directly, with the product code so we know exactly what you have paid for.

You may use a pack with your own classes for as long as you teach, print the slides as handouts, and adapt them. You may not resell it, upload it to a sharing site, or pass the Drive link to another teacher - one purchase is for one teacher.

blocks.heading: Using slides well in a crowded classroom
text: A projector changes what a lesson can do, and it changes what can go wrong. These are worth knowing whether the slides are ours or your own.
bullets: **Do not read the slide aloud.** The class can read it. Say the thing the slide does not say.
**One idea to a slide.** A slide holding four points is a slide nobody finishes reading before you move on.
**Leave the task slide up** while the class works. The commonest reason a pupil sits doing nothing is that the instruction has gone from the screen.
**Check the back row can read it** before the lesson, not during it. If you cannot read a slide from the back of your own classroom, neither can they.
**Have a paper plan too.** Electricity fails, and a lesson that only exists on a screen stops with it.

blocks.title: Free first
